capabilities: Download video or audio-only files from a pasted URL via local yt-dlp
Insert the downloaded attachment and source link into the active note
Replace right-clicked raw URLs or Markdown links with downloaded media
Show download progress in the status bar and an activity panel with diagnostics
Follow Obsidian's configured attachment location or a custom media folder
extras: Desktop-only (Obsidian 1.7.2+); not yet in the community plugin directory, so beta installs go through BRAT or manual copy. Includes a prominent responsible-use section stating it must not be used to circumvent DRM, paywalls, or access controls, and does not bundle or update yt-dlp or ffmpeg.
motivation: The author wanted an intentionally narrow tool: existing community plugins either support only Windows, make downloading secondary to a larger player, or focus on transcription and AI.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to save external audio or video as vault attachments, and existing plugins are Windows-only, make downloading a side feature of a media player, or focus on transcription and AI.

relations.evidence: It uses your local yt-dlp installation to save a lecture, webcast, video, or podcast
ffmpeg for merged video streams and audio conversion
For beta testing before directory approval, add through BRAT

summary: Desktop plugin that uses a local yt-dlp installation to download authorized audio and video into the vault as normal attachments.
